You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": "continual_arc_notes.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC pattern notes

## Border-bars + isolated marker rays (task-114588b6)
Observed in three demos and one solved test. Background is the most common color. Two edge segments of an accent color occur on opposite sides (e.g. right edge vertical segment and left edge vertical segment), plus isolated pixels of a third color. For each isolated pixel lying on a row aligned to one edge segment, extend a horizontal ray from that pixel toward the segment's edge. Replace the isolated pixel itself with color 4; fill the cells between it and the edge with the isolated pixel's original color; preserve the edge-bar cells. The matching segment on the opposite side gets full horizontal fill in the isolated-pixel color on rows corresponding to the marker rows by the constant offset between the two bar segments; preserve the border-bar pixel. Rows in the edge segments with no corresponding marker stay unchanged.

Example (demo 3, 20x15): bg=3, border color=1; right bar rows 1–8 at col14, left bar rows 12–19 at col0. Markers color9 at (1,8),(2,8),(4,3),(5,6),(8,6). Output marks each source at its location with 4 and fills from there rightward to col13 with 9, preserving col14=1. Opposite rows 12,13,15,16,19 are filled 9 from col1 through col14, preserving col0=1. Correspondence offset is +11. Other rows unchanged.

Demo 1 confirms same rule with bg6, border9, markers color5, edge segments right rows2–6 / left rows18–22: source rows 2 and 6 ray rightward, opposite rows18 and22 fill rightward from left edge. Demo 2 shows analogous orthogonal arrangement: top/right and left-side border segments; markers extend horizontally toward the adjacent edge, and matching opposite segment rows fill.

Caution: while the solved instance submission used the inferred rule, its first submitted grid was marked incorrect, so re-check all indices carefully when applying. Likely easy pitfalls: bar segment inclusive endpoints, correspondence offset, preserve border color; source marker becomes 4, not original color. Original task test had bg7, right-edge bar color5 on rows2–8 col23, left-edge bar color5 rows21–27 col0; color3 markers at (2,11),(3,4),(5,9),(7,14),(8,6). A later answer was accepted after a corrected full-grid submission; replay carefully rather than blindly trusting the first attempted grid.
"
